connection_condition: transactions_1k.CustomerID corresponds to customers.CustomerID; every transaction line resolves to exactly one customer and no transaction line lacks a customer
description: A transaction is a component of a customer's purchase activity; a transaction line cannot exist without an owning customer.
A transaction is a component of the activity of the gas station where it took place; the station determines the transaction's country.
A transaction line records the purchase of a component product from the catalogue.

connection_condition: products.ProductID and products.Description are two representations of the same product record
description: A product and its description denote the same catalogue entry; analytical needs phrased with product names must be resolved through the description column because names are not unique.
A station is a component of a chain; every station carries a chain identifier, while the chain has no independent table.
A station is located in a country, recorded as a plain text attribute on the station rather than a reference to a country table.
A station carries a market segment attribute taken from the station-specific segment value domain.
A customer is classified into a business segment recorded as a plain text attribute on the customer.
A customer settles payments in one currency recorded as a plain text attribute on the customer.

connection_condition: The SME subset is the set of customers whose customer_segment value equals 'SME', a subset of the three customer segment values
description: SME customers are an instance-level subset of the customer segment dimension; the SME value domain is contained in the customer segment value domain.

connection_condition: yearmonth.CustomerID corresponds to customers.CustomerID; every consumption record resolves to exactly one customer
description: A monthly consumption record is a component of a customer's consumption history and has no meaning without its customer.
Each consumption value is attributed to the year-month period recorded alongside it; period is a plain text attribute of the record rather than a reference to a calendar table.

connection_condition: Both dimensions express calendar time but in different granularity and text format: transaction dates are day-level 'YYYY-MM-DD' values while period values are month-level 'YYYYMM' values
description: Transaction dates and consumption periods describe time over the same business calendar but are stored independently and cannot be joined directly.

Payment currency and gas station country are parallel geographic groupings over the same business, but no structural connection exists between them: currency is an attribute of customers while country is an attribute of stations, and the customer table carries no country.
Two unrelated segmentation dimensions share the column name Segment in different tables with disjoint value domains; they must be distinguished by their owning table rather than by the name alone.
Average price per unit is derived using the customer's total transaction price as its numerator.
Average price per unit is derived using the customer's total purchased amount as its denominator, so the ratio must be formed from aggregated totals rather than per-line values.
Customer total spending is the aggregation of the transaction price measure over all transaction lines belonging to that customer.

The currency customer ratio is computed from the counts of customers in each currency group, or equivalently as a difference between those counts when a question asks how many more customers use one currency.
